bib.title: WebThinker: Empowering Large Reasoning Models with Deep Research Capability
bib.venue: 39th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2025)

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed only; case-study tables 4-10 read.

question: How can a large reasoning model be given autonomous web search, page navigation and report-drafting abilities inside its own reasoning chain, and does that beat RAG workflows and Search-o1 on hard research tasks?
hypothesis: Letting the reasoning model itself decide when to search, click through pages and draft report sections (instead of a predefined RAG workflow), then tuning tool use with iterative online DPO, improves problem solving and report quality.
contributions: WebThinker, a deep research agent that autonomously searches, explores web pages and drafts reports within its thinking process
A Deep Web Explorer that lets LRMs search and navigate by clicking links/buttons
An Autonomous Think-Search-and-Draft strategy with draft, check and edit tools
RL-based training that synthesizes tool-use preference data and applies iterative online DPO
Experiments on QwQ-32B and DeepSeek-R1-distilled backbones

method.summary: A reasoning model (QwQ-32B) emits special tokens to call a Deep Web Explorer (search via Bing API, click via Crawl4AI, summarised by an assistant LLM) and, in report mode, write/check/edit tools run by an assistant LLM over a document memory. The model is further tuned with 2 iterations of online DPO on trajectory preference pairs ranked by correctness, tool-call count and brevity.
method.task: knowledge-intensive question answering (GPQA, GAIA, WebWalkerQA, HLE) and open-ended scientific report generation (Glaive)

datasets.name: GPQA (diamond)
datasets.source: Rein et al. GPQA, 4-option multiple choice

datasets.name: GAIA
datasets.preprocessing: text-only because model cannot handle other modalities

datasets.name: Humanity's Last Exam (HLE)
datasets.split: random sample of text-only questions from 2500

datasets.name: Glaive reasoning-v1-20m
datasets.size: 30 questions for testing; 1.5k questions sampled per iteration for preference data

datasets.name: Preference-data pool (SuperGPQA, WebWalkerQA Silver, OpenThoughts, NaturalReasoning, NuminaMath)
datasets.size: approximately 3k data points sampled in total
datasets.source: SuperGPQA 26,529 q; WebWalkerQA Silver 13.6k; OpenThoughts 114,000; NaturalReasoning 2.8 million; NuminaMath
datasets.preprocessing: keep only questions QwQ-32B cannot answer by direct generation; sample three responses each from WebThinker-32B-Base and filter by the Section 3.5 criteria

models.name: Assistant models
models.init_from: Qwen2.5-Instruct, same parameters as the backbone

other.use: judges answer correctness on all problem-solving tasks

other.note: cold-start SFT on 7.8k QwQ-32B WebThinker trajectories then RL

training.objective: iterative online DPO; preference pairs ranked by (1) correctness or report quality, (2) fewer total tool calls, (3) shorter output when length ratio exceeds gamma > 1

other.offline_DPO_ablation: an offline DPO variant is compared, details not given

inference.decoding: max 81920 tokens, temperature 0.7, top_p 0.8, top_k 20, repetition penalty 1.05
inference.samples: single run, Pass@1; no seeds or error bars reported
inference.prompting: user prompts (not system prompts); QwQ tasks use boxed answer format; non-reasoning baselines get CoT sentence
inference.retrieval: Bing Web Search API (US-EN region, k=10), pages fetched with Crawl4AI; assistant LLM summarises clicked pages

metrics.name: Pass@1
metrics.definition: accuracy judged by Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct; last five lines used as answer if extraction fails

metrics.name: Report quality (Comp., Thorough., Fact., Coherence)
metrics.definition: listwise scores out of 10 from DeepSeek-R1-671B and GPT-4o, averaged; randomized order

baselines: Direct reasoning (Qwen2.5-32B/72B, DeepSeek-R1-32B/671B, QwQ-32B, GPT-4o, o1-preview, o3-mini, Gemini-2.0-Flash-Thinking)
Standard RAG, RAG w/ query planning, iterative RAG (Qwen2.5-32B, QwQ-32B)
eval.protocol: single run, no error bars (NeurIPS checklist: no error bars due to compute cost); report judged by two LLMs, no human evaluation; 30 report questions

prompts.text: Please objectively evaluate the quality of research articles generated by systems A, B, C, D and E for this question, and provide scores out of 10 for the following criteria: (1) Overall Comprehensiveness (2) Thoroughness of Discussion (3) Factuality (4) Coherence
You are an evaluation assistant. Please determine if the predicted answer is equivalent to the labeled answer.

prompts.where: Appendix C.1, Instruction for Search Plan Generation

evidence.quote: Generation uses max 81920 tokens, temperature 0.7, top_p 0.8, top_k 20, and repetition penalty 1.05.

results.claim: WebThinker-32B-RL averages 70.7 on GPQA, versus 67.2 for Search-o1-32B.
results.setup: GPQA diamond, 198 questions, QwQ-32B backbone, judged by Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct, single run
results.table: Table 1, row WebThinker-32B-RL, column GPQA Avg. (Search-o1-32B 67.2)

results.claim: WebThinker-32B-RL scores 48.5 on GAIA versus 39.8 for Search-o1-32B.
results.setup: GAIA text-only validation, 103 questions, QwQ-32B backbone, Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct judge
results.table: Table 1, row WebThinker-32B-RL, column GAIA Avg. (Search-o1-32B 39.8)
results.note: Intro says 21.9% gain over Search-o1, which is a relative gain (48.5/39.8).

results.claim: WebThinker-32B-RL scores 46.5 on WebWalkerQA versus 34.1 for Search-o1-32B.
results.setup: WebWalkerQA test set, 680 questions, QwQ-32B backbone, Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct judge
results.table: Table 1, row WebThinker-32B-RL, column WebWalkerQA Avg. (Search-o1-32B 34.1)

results.claim: WebThinker-32B-RL scores 15.8 on Humanity's Last Exam versus 10.8 for Search-o1-32B.
results.setup: HLE, random 500 text-only questions, QwQ-32B backbone, Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct judge
results.note: Fig 1 prints Search-o1-32B as 11.6 on HLE; Table 2 prints 10.8. The intro claim of 36.2% on HLE matches 15.8/11.6, not 15.8/10.8.

results.claim: Training-free WebThinker-32B-Base also beats Search-o1 on GAIA (44.7), WebWalkerQA (41.9) and HLE (13.0).
results.setup: GAIA text-only validation, Base = no DPO training
results.table: Table 1, row WebThinker-32B-Base, column GAIA Avg.
results.note: Text claims +22.9% on WebWalkerQA and +20.4% on HLE, relative gains.

results.claim: OpenAI Deep Research is quoted at 67.4 average on GAIA (Level 1 74.3, Level 2 69.1, Level 3 47.6) and 26.6 on HLE, from official releases.
results.source: OpenAI Deep Research official release (dagger in Table 1 and 2)
results.setup: GAIA as reported by OpenAI (question set not stated in this paper; probably not the 103-question text-only subset); HLE 26.6 on whatever HLE set OpenAI used; no GPQA or WebWalkerQA numbers
results.table: Table 1, row OpenAI Deep Research, column GAIA Avg.; Table 2, row OpenAI Deep Research, column Avg. (26.6)
results.note: Not comparable with WebThinker's own 103/500-question subsets.

results.claim: Online DPO training raises problem-solving average from 42.1 (Base) to 45.4 (RL); offline DPO gives 43.2.
results.metric: average over GPQA, GAIA, WebWalkerQA, HLE
results.setup: Table 3 ablation, QwQ-32B backbone, average of four benchmarks
results.table: Table 3 left, rows WebThinker-32B-RL, w/ Offline DPO, w/o Training (Base), column Avg.
results.note: Text in Sec 4.7 prints the RL average as 44.9; Table 3 prints 45.4 (mean of 70.7, 48.5, 46.5, 15.8 is 45.4).

results.claim: RL training has minimal effect on report quality: average 8.1 trained versus 8.0 untrained.
results.setup: Glaive, 30 test questions, judged by DeepSeek-R1-671B and GPT-4o averaged
results.quote: Its impact on report generation is minimal, as the base framework is already effective.

results.claim: Removing the Deep Web Explorer drops problem-solving average to 38.3 and report average to 7.7.
results.quote: Removing the Deep Web Explorer severely degrades both problem-solving (Avg. 38.3) and report generation (Avg. 7.7)

results.claim: Removing autonomous report drafting gives the largest report-quality drop (average 6.6 versus 8.1).
results.quote: Removing autonomous drafting causes the largest quality drop in report generation (Avg. 6.6)

results.claim: WebThinker-32B-RL reaches report average 8.1 (Base 8.0) versus Gemini2.0 Deep Research 7.9 and Grok3 DeeperSearch 6.5.
results.setup: Glaive, 30 questions; listwise judging by DeepSeek-R1-671B and GPT-4o, scores averaged; no error bars, no human evaluation; competitor systems' reports presumably obtained by running them (not stated)
results.table: Table in Sec 4.5 / Fig 4, rows WebThinker-32B-RL, Gemini2.0 Deep Research, column Avg.
results.note: Text says WebThinker achieves top overall score 8.0 (Base); RL row is 8.1. Differences of 0.1 to 0.2 on 30 questions with no variance reported.

results.claim: RL-trained WebThinker beats o3-mini (High) on HLE (15.8 vs 14.0).
results.setup: HLE; o3-mini (High) figure is from official releases, set may differ from the 500-question sample
results.quote: Notably, on HLE, it surpasses even stronger models like o3-mini (High).

results.claim: WebThinker-R1-7B gains 174.4% (GAIA) and 422.6% (WebWalkerQA) relative over direct generation.
results.setup: DeepSeek-R1-7B backbone after cold-start SFT on 7.8k trajectories then RL
results.quote: WebThinker-R1-7B achieved relative gains of 174.4% (GAIA) and 422.6% (WebWalkerQA)

limits: Authors concede: cannot process images or video; supports only a limited tool set; no GUI-based web exploration.
No error bars or multiple seeds (checklist: too costly); gaps like 8.1 vs 7.9 on 30 report questions are not tested for significance.
Report quality judged only by LLMs (DeepSeek-R1-671B, GPT-4o); authors argue against human evaluation because system origin is easy to identify.
OpenAI Deep Research numbers are official-release figures, not run on the same GAIA/HLE subsets.
DPO hyperparameters (beta, lr, batch size, n samples, gamma), hardware and compute are not given despite the checklist saying they are.
Text and table disagree: RL average 44.9 vs 45.4; Search-o1 HLE 11.6 (Fig 1) vs 10.8 (Table 2).
Live Bing search and web content change over time, so reruns will differ (inferred).

terms.definition: LRM-driven tool that searches, clicks links/buttons and extracts relevant information, returning a concise summary to the main reasoning chain
the LRM interleaves reasoning, searching and drafting report sections using draft, check and edit tools

lineage.work: Search-o1: Agentic search-enhanced large reasoning models

lineage.note: iterative online DPO for tool use
eval and Silver set for training
trained on Wikipedia-based QA; WebThinker targets real-world web and reports
